findings.finding: The Q2 release and call (2026-07-23) set up an H2 acceleration that the stock has since given back: organic orders +16% (PA&T orders +24%, book-to-bill >1.2; Building Automation orders +13%), backlog ~$20B (+9%), H2 organic growth guided 4-6% vs 3-4% FY, management calling a 'sharp inflection' in PA&T growth from Q3 and H2 catalyst volumes +25-30% vs H1, CEO describing the guide as carrying 'a level of prudence' and CFO saying there is 'more room' to beat the raised guide in Q3 and Q4; the bar ($2.15) is only 2.5c above the guide midpoint, so a print at or above the top ($2.20) plus a firmed/raised FY range is the base case the commentary points to.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-23): beat ($1.95 vs $1.80 consensus) and FY EPS raise outweighed a below-street Q3 guide and the stock rose +5.7% (baseline) / +7.3% (MarketBeat). Prior-perimeter prints (history flagged untrustworthy): +6.81% Oct-2025, +4.89% Jan-2026, -2.56% Apr-2026 on a revenue miss. Beats with a raise have been bought, not sold.
findings.why_not_priced: If the H2 acceleration were priced the stock would sit near its post-Q2 level (~$243 on 2026-07-27, CEO-level Form 4 price) rather than $213.67, 18% under the 52w high and below its 50/200-day averages (~$226.5 in mid-September); instead it de-rated on the Aerospace sister company's supply-chain miss and cautious August conference talk, with a Hold downgrade at $190. The guide is public, but the market is paying a discount on whether it is conservative.
